assessment: The authors use human trisomy and tetrasomy 21 cell lines and a mouse model to examine the effects of an additional copy of Pericentrin (PCNT) on cell biology, with a focus on ciliation and ciliary Hedgehog signaling. They demonstrate that modestly increased PCNT levels can attenuate ciliogenesis and may result in trisomy 21-associated phenotypes such as cerebellar growth defects. This work advances our understanding of the trafficking defects caused by increased PCNT and has important implications for our understanding of the cellular basis of trisomy 21, a major hereditary human disorder.
